headline_marked: Body of [[Bangladeshi killed in Israeli drone strike]] reaches Satkhira
headline: Body of Bangladeshi killed in Israeli drone strike reaches Satkhira
summary: Shuvo Kumar Das, who went to Lebanon to support his family, was killed in a drone attack near the Israel border. His body was returned to Bangladesh after four months.
details: The body of Shuvo Kumar Das, a Bangladeshi national killed in an Israeli drone strike in Lebanon, has returned to his home in Sripatipura village, Kalaroa Upazila, Satkhira.

Shuvo was killed on May 11 in the Maifadun area of southern Lebanon, near the Israel border, while at his workplace. His body was recovered two days later with the help of the Lebanese Army and the Red Cross.
To send Shuvo abroad, his father, a van driver, sold land and borrowed 4 lakh BDT from local lenders at high interest rates. The family now lives in a rented house.
Shuvo worked as a caretaker for a house and fruit garden in Lebanon, sending home approximately 35,000 BDT per month to pay off loans and support his siblings' education.
His mother, Shikha Rani Das, shared that Shuvo had gone to Lebanon unmarried to improve the family's financial situation, and they had hoped to bring him home for marriage.
The return of the body took four months due to security concerns and lack of full government control in the conflict zone where he was killed.
The family has received 85,000 BDT from the airport. They may receive further government assistance of up to 13 lakh BDT, depending on the verification of his BMET registration and travel dates.
Kalaroa UNO Ariful Islam stated that the rescue and repatriation process was delayed due to the war situation near the Israel border.
caption:
A father sold his land and borrowed 4 lakh BDT to send his son to Lebanon. Now, the son has returned home in a coffin.

The body of Shuvo Kumar Das, a Bangladeshi national killed in an Israeli drone strike in Lebanon, has returned to his home in Sripatipura village, Kalaroa Upazila, Satkhira.

Shuvo was killed on May 11 in the Maifadun area of southern Lebanon, near the Israel border, while at his workplace. His body was recovered two days later with the help of the Lebanese Army and the Red Cross.

To send Shuvo abroad, his father, a van driver, sold land and borrowed 4 lakh BDT from local lenders at high interest rates. The family now lives in a rented house.

Shuvo worked as a caretaker for a house and fruit garden in Lebanon, sending home approximately 35,000 BDT per month to pay off loans and support his siblings' education.

His mother, Shikha Rani Das, shared that Shuvo had gone to Lebanon unmarried to improve the family's financial situation, and they had hoped to bring him home for marriage.

The return of the body took four months due to security concerns and lack of full government control in the conflict zone where he was killed.

The family has received 85,000 BDT from the airport. They may receive further government assistance of up to 13 lakh BDT, depending on the verification of his BMET registration and travel dates.

Kalaroa UNO Ariful Islam stated that the rescue and repatriation process was delayed due to the war situation near the Israel border.

headline: Sheikh Hasina and 11 others charge-sheeted in Riazul murder case
summary: The former Prime Minister and 11 other individuals have been officially named in the charge sheet for the murder of Riazul.
details: Sheikh Hasina, the former Prime Minister of Bangladesh, has been charge-sheeted along with 11 other individuals in connection with the murder of Riazul.
The charge sheet is part of an ongoing legal process to hold those responsible for the killing of Riazul accountable.
This development comes amid a broader context of legal actions being taken against former government officials and leaders.
